user_stories.story: As an employee, I upload a file to a work folder and see scan, sync, retention, and sharing status before colleagues can access it.
As an admin, I enforce tenant and regional sharing policy so public links, external recipients, and DLP exceptions are denied or audited deterministically.
As a compliance officer, I place files or folders under legal hold and export immutable evidence without relying on manual operator access.
As an integrator, I react to Drive file lifecycle events through Workflow and Ontology contracts instead of direct cross-product database calls.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user uploads a file into a tenant workspace folder
acceptance_criteria.then: the file is stored with tenant/context metadata, immutable content hash, object-store version, retention class, and audit-chain event before it becomes visible

acceptance_criteria.given: a file requires virus scan or DLP evaluation
acceptance_criteria.when: a viewer, search indexer, preview renderer, or share link attempts access before the scan verdict is clean or policy-approved
acceptance_criteria.then: access is denied or quarantined with a policy-safe explanation and audit event

acceptance_criteria.given: a user creates a share link or grants a permission
acceptance_criteria.when: the requested recipient, TTL, geography, or data class violates tenant/regional policy
acceptance_criteria.then: Cedar-backed authorization denies the grant, records the denial, and never emits a usable link token

acceptance_criteria.given: a file or folder is under legal hold or WORM compliance mode
acceptance_criteria.when: a delete, retention-expiry, overwrite, or folder move attempts to remove protected evidence
acceptance_criteria.then: the mutation is blocked, the hold relationship remains intact, and an immutable audit event references the protected object version

acceptance_criteria.given: a user syncs Drive changes across devices
acceptance_criteria.when: two devices modify the same file or folder path concurrently
acceptance_criteria.then: sync produces deterministic conflict artifacts, preserves both contents, and emits a conflict-resolution event without data loss

acceptance_criteria.given: a search or preview request targets a file the principal cannot read
acceptance_criteria.when: index rows or rendered previews are queried
acceptance_criteria.then: the response reveals neither content, snippets, metadata, nor thumbnail side channels beyond allowed minimum disclosure

acceptance_criteria.given: a Drive file lifecycle event is produced
acceptance_criteria.when: Workflow, Ontology, or downstream workplace apps need to react
acceptance_criteria.then: the handoff uses typed contracts/events and never requires a direct cross-product database read

cross_product_routing_policy.policy_ref: ADR-0131/ADR-0512 source-root authority plus workflow/ontology contracts

invariants: file not visible outside policy before required scan verdict
move cannot bypass legal hold or tenant boundary
no link token is materialized on policy deny
revocation cascades to derived preview/download tokens
cross-context grant requires explicit Workflow/policy basis
protected object versions cannot be overwritten or deleted
release requires configured two-person or legal process

persistence.retention: per jurisdiction, legal hold, and object version policy
follows source file; purge or tombstone on delete/hold release
bounded device/session lifetime with audit-safe reset

privacy_and_threat_boundaries.default_policy: deny-by-default for cross-tenant, cross-context, scan-pending, legal-hold, public-link, and regional-transfer-sensitive reads

attacker_models.goal: reuse, guess, or extend share-link access after revocation or TTL expiry
controls: no token materialization on policy deny

attacker_models.goal: exfiltrate regulated files through preview, search snippet, or sync side channel
delete or alter held evidence outside legal process
read arbitrary tenant data or emit unsafe artifacts

stride.spoofing: upload, share, and permission mutations require authenticated principal/context and idempotency keys
stride.tampering: content hashes and object version refs make file mutation append-only at the evidence layer
stride.repudiation: share, scan, hold, denial, and permission events emit audit-chain evidence
stride.information_disclosure: search, preview, sync, and share-link reads are authorization-trimmed and scan-aware
stride.denial_of_service: multipart upload, preview, scan, and sync queues need per-tenant quotas and backpressure
stride.elevation_of_privilege: permission inheritance and ownership transfer are Cedar/RBAC checked and deny by default

privacy_boundaries: personal files never become employer-visible without explicit user action and policy basis
work files remain tenant-scoped and subject to retention, legal hold, and admin policy
search snippets, thumbnails, and preview derivatives inherit source-file authorization and retention
DLP/virus scan evidence stores minimum necessary verdict metadata; raw sensitive content is not copied into audit logs

optimization_practices.implementation: every upload commit records a content hash and immutable object version before mutable metadata points at it
search and preview derivatives inherit source-file policy and never expose unauthorized snippets or thumbnails
upload commit, permission change, share-link mint/revoke, and legal-hold mutations carry idempotency keys and emit replayable events
upload, preview, scan, and sync queues expose retry_after and per-tenant quota class
conflicting writes preserve both object versions and use stable tie-break labels for user-visible resolution

risks.risk: share link exposes regulated or tenant-confidential file outside policy
risks.mitigation: Cedar-backed deny-by-default share-link minting, strict TTL, recipient scope, revocation cascade, and no-token-on-deny invariant

risks.risk: DLP or malware scan is bypassed by preview, search, sync, or direct download path
risks.mitigation: scan-pending quarantine state is checked by every read/derivative surface before visibility

risks.risk: legal-hold or WORM evidence is deleted through object overwrite, folder move, or retention expiry
risks.mitigation: immutability-tier blocks protected mutations and anchors object-version refs in audit-chain evidence

risks.risk: search snippet, thumbnail, or sync metadata leaks file content to unauthorized principals
risks.mitigation: authorization-trimmed indexes, preview policy checks, minimum-disclosure errors, and side-channel tests

risks.risk: large uploads, previews, or scan queues create noisy-neighbor saturation
risks.mitigation: per-tenant quotas, backpressure, admission control, and capacity SLO burn alerts
